corpus_definition: To say that something is good and worth having.

forms.definition: advice that something is good or that someone should try it
forms.example: We chose this hotel on a friend's recommendation.

syn.note: An idea someone gives you; a little weaker than a recommendation.
Related: an opinion about what you should do. Advice is uncountable: 'some advice'.
Related and informal: a small, useful piece of advice.

forms.definition: to tell someone that a thing is good and worth trying
forms.example: Can you recommend a good place to eat in Bukhara?
forms.note: Pattern: recommend something to someone, not 'recommend someone something'.

syn.note: Easy and common; suggest is a little less strong.
Advise is about what someone should do: 'I advise you to rest.'
Related: to say good things about something, but not always telling others to try it.
Formal: to say publicly that you support a product or person.

forms.definition: said by people to be good or worth trying
forms.example: This restaurant is highly recommended by tourists.

syn.note: Related: officially accepted as good or correct.
Related: liked by many people, but nobody has to suggest it.

forms.note: No adverb in this family.

context.text: My teacher recommended a good English book. I followed her recommendation, and now I read a few pages every evening.

reviewer_note: No false re- split: commend is not taught as the base for learners, so no prefix is claimed.

corpus_definition: to become healthy again after being sick or hurt
particle_note: Not separable: recover from + noun: 'recover from the flu', 'recover from an operation'. Also used for bad events: 'recover from a shock'.

relations.note: Everyday phrasal verb with the same meaning: 'get over a cold'.
Easy and common, but used without 'from': 'He is getting better.'
Formal: to rest and become strong again after an illness.
Related: used mostly for wounds and injuries: 'The cut healed quickly.'
To become more ill instead of healthier.

context.text: My little brother had a bad cold last week, but he recovered from it in three days. Doctors say most children recover from the flu quickly.

reviewer_note: Fixed verb + preposition; recover itself (with recovery) is a separate headword.

corpus_definition: Turning old items into new materials to use again.

forms.definition: the process of making used things into new material
forms.example: Recycling helps to keep our streets and parks clean.

syn.note: Related: using something again in the same form, without making new material from it.
Related and technical: treating used material so it can be used again.

forms.definition: to make used paper, glass or plastic into new material
forms.example: We recycle paper and glass at our school.

syn.note: Related: to use something again, often without changing it.
Related and technical: to treat used material so it can be used again.

ant.note: To put something in the rubbish instead of using it again.

forms.definition: able to be made into new material after it is used
forms.example: Most plastic bottles are recyclable.

syn.note: Related: can be used again, often in the same form, like a shopping bag.

ant.note: Made to be used once and then thrown away.

forms.definition: made from material that was used before
forms.example: This notebook is made of recycled paper.

forms.note: No adverb in this family.

context.text: In Tashkent, many families now recycle plastic bottles. Recycling is easy when there is a special bin for recyclable things near your home.

reviewer_note: Headword is the -ing noun; recycle is the verb it comes from. Compounds like recycling bin left out.

corpus_definition: To make someone feel less tired or hot.

forms.definition: food and drink, or the good feeling of being less tired
forms.example: Light refreshments will be served after the meeting.
forms.note: Usually plural: refreshments = snacks and drinks at an event.

syn.note: Related: a small amount of food between meals.
Related: a time when you relax and feel less tired.

forms.definition: to make someone feel less tired, hot or thirsty
forms.example: A cold drink will refresh you after the long walk.
forms.note: Also used for computers: refresh a web page = load it again.

syn.note: To give someone energy again; a little stronger.
Related: to make someone less hot.
Related and informal: to make someone feel more awake.
Related: to give someone a lot of energy. British spelling: energise.

ant.note: To make someone feel that they need rest.

forms.definition: making you feel less tired or hot
forms.example: We had a refreshing swim in the lake.
forms.note: Also means 'pleasantly new and different': 'a refreshing change'.

syn.note: Formal: making you feel full of energy.
Related: a little cold in a pleasant way.
Related: nice and enjoyable, but not always about energy.

ant.note: Making you feel that you need rest.

forms.definition: feeling less tired after rest, food or drink
forms.example: I woke up feeling refreshed after a good sleep.

syn.note: Less tired after sleep or a break.

forms.definition: in a pleasant way because it is new or different
forms.example: Her answer was refreshingly honest.
forms.note: Belongs to refreshing = pleasantly new and different, not about feeling less tired.

context.text: A cold drink really refreshes you after a long walk in the hills near Chorvoq. The mountain air there is refreshing too.

reviewer_note: refreshingly kept as other_meaning (new and different), not hidden. No re- split claimed (refresh is not 'fresh again' for learners).

corpus_definition: A person who is part of your family.

forms.definition: a person who is a member of your family
forms.example: I invited all my relations to the wedding.
forms.note: Relative is more common in everyday English. Relation also means 'connection': 'the relation between diet and health'.

syn.note: Easy phrase with the same meaning.
Old-fashioned and formal: your family as a group.

ant.note: A person you do not know and who is not part of your family.

forms.definition: the way two people or groups feel and behave towards each other
forms.example: She has a good relationship with her boss.
forms.note: Belongs to relation = connection between people, not a family member.

forms.definition: to show or see a connection between two things
forms.example: It is hard to relate these two ideas.
forms.note: Belongs to relation = connection. For family, English uses the adjective: 'We are related.'

forms.definition: belonging to the same family
forms.example: Are you and Aziz related? You look very similar.
forms.note: Pattern: be related to someone.

syn.note: Related: joined in some way, not only by family.

forms.definition: true when compared with other things
forms.example: They live in relative comfort.
forms.note: Belongs to relation = connection or comparison. The noun relative (a family member) is shown in People & things.

forms.definition: quite, when compared with other things
forms.example: The test was relatively easy.
forms.note: False friend: belongs to relative = compared with others, nothing to do with family.

people.definition: a person who is part of your family
people.example: We visit our relatives in Namangan every summer.

context.text: All my relations came to my sister's wedding in Andijan. Some of them were distant relatives I had never met, but we are all related.

reviewer_note: Headword is a person noun, so it stays the noun main entry and relative goes in People & things (not a synonym). relatively is a false friend.

corpus_definition: The way two people or groups feel and act toward each other.

forms.definition: the way two people or groups feel and behave towards each other
forms.example: They have a very strong relationship.
forms.note: Also means a romantic connection: 'She is in a relationship.'

syn.note: A strong feeling that joins people: 'a close bond'.
Related: a link between people or things.
Related: one kind of relationship, between friends.

forms.definition: the way countries or groups behave towards each other
forms.example: Relations between the two countries are friendly.
forms.note: In this meaning usually plural: relations.

syn.note: Plural noun for the links between countries or groups: 'close ties'.

forms.definition: to understand someone's feelings and get on well with them
forms.example: Many teenagers find it hard to relate to their parents.
forms.note: Pattern: relate to someone.

syn.note: To feel that you understand someone because you are similar.
Related and easy: to know how someone feels.
Related: to have a friendly relationship. 'get on with someone'.

forms.definition: connected in some way, or from the same family
forms.example: We discussed the problem and other related issues.
forms.note: Belongs to relation = connection or family, not to how people behave towards each other.

forms.definition: true when compared with other things
forms.example: After the storm, the city returned to relative calm.
forms.note: Belongs to relation = comparison.

forms.definition: quite, when compared with other things
forms.example: The flat is relatively cheap for the city centre.
forms.note: False friend: belongs to relative = compared with others, not to relationships.

people.definition: a person who is part of your family
people.example: Many relatives came to visit during Navruz.
people.note: Belongs to relation = a family member.

context.text: Aziz has a good relationship with his neighbours. He can relate to their problems because his family has the same ones, and relations in the whole street are friendly.

reviewer_note: relation (plural relations = how groups behave) kept as existing extra noun; relatively flagged as a false friend.

corpus_definition: a feeling of comfort when worry or pain goes away

forms.definition: a good feeling when worry or pain stops
forms.example: She felt great relief when she heard the good news.
forms.note: Also means help such as food and money for people after a disaster: 'relief aid'.

syn.note: A feeling of being calm and less worried.
Related: a state with no worry or difficulty.
Related: words or actions that stop someone worrying.

ant.note: The feeling of being afraid that something bad will happen.

forms.definition: to make pain or worry less strong
forms.example: This medicine will relieve your headache.

syn.note: Very close: 'ease the pain'.
To make pain or bad feelings softer and calmer.
Related: to make smaller or less.
Related: to make someone less worried or angry.

ant.note: To make pain or a problem worse.

forms.definition: happy because a worry or problem has gone away
forms.example: I was relieved to find my phone in my bag.

syn.note: Related and easy: happy about something.
Less worried because someone or something has helped.
Related: pleased that something bad did not happen.

ant.note: Feeling that something bad may happen.

forms.note: No adverb in learner dictionaries; English uses 'with relief': 'She smiled with relief.'

context.text: When the doctor said my grandfather was fine, it was a big relief. We were all so relieved, and the medicine soon helped to relieve his pain.

reviewer_note: Spelling trap: relief (noun) vs relieve (verb). No affix claimed (relieve is not re- + lieve).

corpus_definition: To trust that someone will help you.
particle_note: Not separable: rely on + person/thing: 'rely on my friends'. Also rely on someone to do something: 'You can rely on him to be on time.'

relations.note: A little informal: 'You can count on me.'
To believe someone is honest and will not hurt you; no 'on' after it.
Related and informal: to get help and support from someone in a hard time.
To feel that you cannot trust someone.

context.text: My grandmother relies on me to help her with the shopping. In our mahalla, you can always rely on good neighbours.

reviewer_note: Fixed verb + preposition; reliable/reliance belong to the separate headword rely.

corpus_definition: To help someone remember something they might forget.

forms.definition: a message or note that helps you remember something
forms.example: I set a reminder on my phone for the meeting.

syn.note: Related: something that makes you do or say something, often on a computer.
Related: a short piece of writing to help you remember.
Related: a short written message at work.

forms.definition: to help someone not forget something
forms.example: Please remind me to call my mother.
forms.note: Patterns: remind someone to do something; remind someone about something; remind someone of someone = look similar.

syn.note: To help someone remember what to say or do next.
Informal phrase: to help someone remember a fact.
Related and easy: 'Tell me to call her later.'

forms.note: No adjective made from remind. Reminiscent looks similar but comes from reminisce, not from remind.
No adverb in this family.

context.text: My phone sends me a reminder before every English lesson. My mother also reminds me to take my keys when I leave home.

reviewer_note: reminder is the core noun (the message itself), so it sits in the noun slot. No re- split claimed (remind is not mind again for learners).

corpus_definition: To pay money to use something that belongs to someone else.

forms.definition: money you pay each month to live in or use a place
forms.example: We pay rent for our apartment every month.

syn.note: Related: any amount of money that you pay.
Related: money you pay for a service, not usually for a home.

forms.definition: the act of paying to use something, or the money for it
forms.example: Car rental is cheap in this city.

syn.note: British English for paying to use something for a short time: 'bike hire'.
Related and formal: a legal agreement to rent something for a long time.

forms.definition: to pay money to use a home, car or other thing
forms.example: Many students rent a room near the university.
forms.note: Rent out = the owner lets someone use it for money.

syn.note: British English for a short time: 'hire a car', 'hire a bike'.
Formal: to rent for a long time with a legal agreement.
Related: to use something and give it back, but without paying.

ant.note: Buying means you own it; renting means you only pay to use it.

forms.definition: paid for each month and not owned by you
forms.example: They live in a rented flat in the city centre.

syn.note: British English, usually for cars and equipment.
Formal: rented with a legal agreement.

ant.note: Belonging to you because you bought it.

forms.note: No adverb in this family.

people.definition: a person who pays money to use a home or thing
people.example: The renter must pay on the first day of the month.
people.note: Mostly American English; British English usually says tenant.

context.text: My cousin rents a small flat near Chilonzor metro. The rent is not cheap, but the rented flat is close to his university.

reviewer_note: CORPUS: definition is the verb but the example uses the noun rent; map follows the verb and shows the noun as a conversion. Tenant and landlord are not made from rent.
